official_sources.title: GDAL Geotransform Tutorial
official_sources.finding: The six-coefficient affine transform maps pixel/line coordinates to georeferenced coordinates; (0,0) is the upper-left pixel corner and the upper-left pixel center is (0.5,0.5).

official_sources.title: GDAL Raster Data Model affine transform
official_sources.finding: GDAL defines the same affine equations and explicitly distinguishes the raster corner at (0,0) from pixel centers at half-integer coordinates.

official_sources.title: GDALDataset GetGeoTransform
official_sources.finding: GetGeoTransform returns the pixel-to-projection affine coefficients; the identity transform may be returned even when fetching a real transform fails, so success status must be checked.

official_sources.title: GDAL ApplyGeoTransform C API
official_sources.finding: GDALApplyGeoTransform documents the exact affine equations used to map fractional pixel/line positions to X/Y coordinates.

official_sources.title: GDALGeoTransform inverse transform
official_sources.finding: GetInverse explicitly reports failure for an uninvertible transform; inverse raster addressing therefore requires a checked inversion result rather than assumed arithmetic.

official_sources.title: GDAL RFC33 PixelIsPoint interpretation
official_sources.finding: GeoTIFF distinguishes RasterPixelIsArea and RasterPixelIsPoint; PixelIsPoint handling involves a half-pixel offset and historical GDAL behavior created compatibility risk.

official_sources.title: GDAL World File format
official_sources.finding: World files store the X/Y coordinate of the upper-left pixel center, unlike GDAL geotransform GT(0),GT(3), which describe the upper-left pixel corner.

official_sources.title: GDAL world-file to geotransform conversion
official_sources.finding: GDAL documents the half-pixel relationship between world-file center offsets and geotransform corner offsets, including rotation terms.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster info georeferencing inventory
official_sources.finding: gdal raster info reports geotransform, corner coordinates, CRS and data-axis-to-CRS-axis mapping, providing an independent addressing manifest channel.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster pixel-info positioning
official_sources.finding: Pixel-info distinguishes pixel column/line positions from dataset/georeferenced positions and defines X as longitude/easting and Y as latitude/northing.

official_sources.title: gdal_translate georeferencing assignment controls
official_sources.finding: -a_gt and -a_ullr assign or override georeferencing without reprojection; -projwin may also align or expand nearest-neighbour windows to pixel boundaries.

official_sources.title: gdalwarp target-aligned-pixel semantics
official_sources.finding: -tap aligns output extent coordinates to target resolution but explicitly does not necessarily align the output grid with the input grid.

official_sources.title: gdalbuildvrt target alignment
official_sources.finding: VRT target-aligned pixels constrain output extent/resolution arithmetic; this is a derived-grid operation and not proof of source cell identity.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster stack target alignment
official_sources.finding: Target-aligned-pixel behavior is defined through integer extent/resolution ratios, reinforcing that grid origin and resolution must both be pinned.

official_sources.title: GDAL rasterize target grid alignment
official_sources.finding: Rasterization exposes explicit extent, resolution and target-alignment controls; changing these creates a different membership grid.

official_sources.title: GDAL SuggestedWarpOutput algorithm
official_sources.finding: SuggestedWarpOutput estimates destination extent by sampling points along source edges and computes a suggested resolution, so its proposed grid is derived rather than immutable source addressing.

official_sources.title: GDAL OGRSpatialReference axis mapping
official_sources.finding: Data-axis-to-CRS-axis mapping can swap or sign-reverse coordinate axes; a mapping such as [2,1] explicitly represents axis inversion.

official_sources.title: GDAL axis mapping configuration
official_sources.finding: OSR_DEFAULT_AXIS_MAPPING_STRATEGY may be authority-compliant or traditional GIS order, meaning runtime configuration can change tuple interpretation.

official_sources.title: GDAL Python spatial-reference axis strategy
official_sources.finding: The API distinguishes authority-compliant, traditional GIS and custom data-axis mappings and exposes the active strategy for audit.

official_sources.title: PROJ axis-order FAQ
official_sources.finding: PROJ follows authority-defined axis ordering, which can differ from traditional GIS longitude/easting-first conventions.

official_sources.title: PROJ axis orientation
official_sources.finding: PROJ supports explicit axis orientation including east/west, north/south and up/down directions, so axis direction is part of coordinate provenance.

official_sources.title: PROJ CRS-to-CRS API axis behavior
official_sources.finding: When AUTHORITY:CODE CRS definitions are used, proj_create_crs_to_crs expects and emits coordinates in the official axis order and units.

official_sources.title: gdaltransform axis-order requirement
official_sources.finding: An explicit coordinate-operation pipeline supplied to gdaltransform must account for source and target CRS axis order.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster calc pixel-center coordinates
official_sources.finding: Raster calc exposes pixel-center X/Y variables in dataset CRS, confirming center coordinates as an explicit raster-position concept.
